Drummer Alvin Queen was born on August 16, 1950 in Mount Vernon, NY. He received invaluable education in the clubs and musicians’ gatherings of New York City. Alvin benefited from the wisdom of drummers Art Blakey, Philly Joe Jones and especially Elvin Jones, and he was performing with Horace Silver at the age of 18. Stints with George Benson, Stanley Turrentine and many others followed. A European tour with trumpeter Charles Tolliver led to his settling in Switzerland in 1978. Alvin is currently the most active drummer on the European jazz scene, and he frequently travels to other continents to perform with artists such as Sweets Edison, Clark Terry and Junior Mance. His own record label, Nilva Records, has released albums by leading European artists as well as Alvin’s own quartet.
Alvin was interviewed during one of his rare visits to the U.S. on August 23, 1997. The interview took place with Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive, at Hamilton College in Clinton.
My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. It’s a real pleasure to have Alvin Queen with us today.
It’s a pleasure to be here, Monk.
Welcome to Central New York. You’re a man who crosses the international date line a lot, from what you’ve said. Do you like traveling that much?
